adults.title: More Than a Signature
adults.big_idea: The Savior invites us not merely to add His name to ours but to take it upon us by covenant, and we do that by serving Him through lifting, loving, and serving others, which changes our hearts.
adults.objective: Learners will explain the difference between adding the Savior’s name and taking it upon them, and will choose one specific person to serve this week as a way of keeping that covenant.
prepare: Read Elder Fantone’s talk, Take upon Us His Name, and mark the three stories: the school form, his parents’ home, and the missionaries.
Write two headings on the board: Add His name / Take upon us His name.
Bring paper and pens for silent writing.
Pray by name for the people you will teach and ask what they need from this lesson.

segments.name: What is in a name?
steps: Begin with prayer. Then ask learners to turn to a neighbor and answer the first question below. Give them two minutes.

Briefly retell Elder Fantone’s story: at a school registrar’s office he was asked to write his daughter’s name, wrote his own by mistake, and fixed it by adding Amanda in front, because her name is Amanda James Fantone.
Explain that later, in a quiet moment, he saw a contrast between that quick fix and the Savior’s invitation. Tell the class that today’s lesson explores that contrast.
questions: Think of a name you carry, such as a family name or a name you were given to honor someone. What does carrying that name ask of you?

segments.name: Add or take upon?
steps: Invite someone to read the first two key quotes below aloud, one after the other.
Divide into groups of three or four. Assign each group one passage: Moroni 6:3; Mosiah 5:8; or 3 Nephi 27:5. Ask them to read it and look for what taking the Savior’s name involves.
Ask each group to send one person to the board to write a few words under the heading where their discovery belongs.
Discuss the questions below. Let learners do most of the talking.
questions: Elder Fantone says the invitation is not to wear His name like a badge of religious affiliation. In ordinary life, what is the difference between a badge and a becoming?
What word or phrase in your passage shows that taking His name is something we keep doing, not something we did once?

segments.name: A home with open doors
steps: Read Mosiah 2:17 together. Point out that Elder Fantone calls this verse the divine key to serving the Lord.

Retell the story of his parents. They lived in a modest three-bedroom bungalow. When his mother, a public school teacher, learned that a recently graduated student could not continue his vocational studies because his family could not afford housing near the school, his parents gave the student the boys’ room. In another season, when the ward Relief Society president spoke of a vulnerable family whose children needed a safe place to stay, his parents opened their doors and some of the children moved into his sisters’ room.
Share Elder Fantone’s conviction that if Joseph and Mary had knocked on their door, and both rooms were already taken, his parents would have gladly offered their own room.
Read President Romney’s words from the aligned quotes, then ask the questions below.
questions: What did these parents’ choices teach their son about whose name they had taken upon them?
President Romney says service is not something we endure to earn a reward. How does that change the way you see the service already in your week?
When has someone made room for you? What did it show you about the Savior?

segments.name: Time did not change
steps: Tell the story of the missionaries. As a mission president, Elder Fantone met some in their first months who were in tears, sad, lonely, and homesick. They prayed, put on their name tags, and went out to serve anyway. A year later the same missionaries sat in his office with glowing faces and did not want their missions to end.
Read the third key quote below. Then read Alma 5:14 and Mosiah 5:13 aloud.
Give everyone paper. Invite two minutes of silent writing on the first question below, then invite a few to share what they are willing to share.
Read the quote from President Farnes in the aligned quotes as a second witness that people are the Lord’s work.
questions: When has serving someone changed you, even though your circumstances stayed the same?
According to Mosiah 5:13, what happens to our relationship with the Master when we do not serve Him? What does that suggest about how we come to know Him?

segments.name: Choose one name
steps: Read the last key quote below, Elder Fantone’s testimony of what we find when we lose our lives in the Savior’s service.
Invite learners to write the name of one person the Spirit brings to mind and one specific thing they will do for that person before next Sunday.
As a check for understanding, ask two or three learners to finish this sentence in their own words: Adding His name is different from taking it upon me because...
questions: Who is knocking at your door right now, and what would it look like to open it?

segments.name: Witness and follow-up
steps: Bear your testimony that the Savior lives and that we come to know Him as we serve Him.
Tell the class that next week you will begin by asking what happened when they served the person whose name they wrote, and what they noticed in themselves.

key_quotes.text: The Savior’s invitation is not merely for us to add His name to our name like a badge of religious affiliation.
His invitation is for us to take upon us His name. It is an invitation to become more like Him through covenant keeping.
Time did not change—the missionaries did.
as we lose our lives in His service, we will find Him and we will find ourselves.

scriptures.use: Read in a small group; look for what those who were baptized were determined to do, and for how long.
One group reads verse 8 for what taking the name means; the whole class reads verse 13 later and discusses how we come to know the Master.
Read together before the story of Elder Fantone’s parents; ask how this verse turns ordinary help into service to God.
Read aloud after the missionary story; ask learners to name the change the missionaries experienced.

aligned_quotes.text: Service is not something we endure on this earth so we can earn the right to live in the celestial kingdom. Service is the very fiber of which an exalted life in the celestial kingdom is made
aligned_quotes.speaker: President Marion G. Romney
President Farnes
aligned_quotes.text: To Jesus, these people were not interrupting His mission. They were His mission.

takeaways: The Savior asks me to take His name upon me, not just add it to mine.
I take His name by serving Him to the end, and I serve Him by serving the people around me.
Service changes me: as I lose my life in His service, I find Him and I find myself.
act: Serve the one person whose name you wrote down, in the specific way you chose, before next Sunday.
During the sacrament, listen for the words about His name and silently tell Heavenly Father one way you will serve His Son this week.
On a day you do not feel like serving, pray first and then go anyway, as the missionaries did. Notice what changes in you.
Ask your family or a friend: who needs room made for them right now? Decide together what to do.
adapt: At home: skip the groups. Read Moroni 6:3 and Mosiah 2:17 together, tell the story of the open home, and choose one person to serve as a household.
Large class: have pairs, not groups, read the passages, and take only one comment per question so you still reach the silent writing.
Short on time: keep Add or take upon, the story of the parents, and Choose one name.

youth.title: Wear the Name, Live the Name
youth.big_idea: Taking the name of Jesus Christ upon us is more than wearing a label; it is a covenant to serve Him, and when we serve others, even when it is hard, He changes us.
youth.objective: Youth will be able to explain in their own words what it means to take the Savior’s name upon them and will plan one act of service to do this week, even if they do not feel like it.
prepare: Read Elder Fantone’s talk, Take upon Us His Name, especially the stories of the school form and the missionaries.
Bring a marker for the board, small cards or slips of paper, and pens.
Write four references on the board: 3 Nephi 27:5; Moroni 6:3; Mosiah 2:17; Mosiah 5:13.
Ask the youth to have scriptures or the Gospel Library app ready.

segments.name: Sign here
steps: As youth arrive, hand each a card and have them sign their name with the hand they do not usually write with. Give ten seconds. Enjoy the results together.

Tell Elder Fantone’s story: at a school office he was asked to write his daughter’s name on a form, and he confidently wrote and signed his own. He fixed it by adding Amanda in front, because her name is Amanda James Fantone.
Say that the quick fix made him think about a bigger question, and ask the question below. Take two or three fast answers.
questions: What is actually in a name? When does a name on a jersey, a uniform, or a form really mean something?

segments.name: Badge or becoming
steps: Have one youth read the first key quote below and another read the second.

In pairs, give two minutes to list on the back of their card what wearing the Savior’s name only as a badge might look like at school, online, or at home, and what truly taking it upon us might look like in the same places. Ask them to describe choices, not people.
Invite each pair to share one contrast. Write a few on the board.
questions: Why do you think the Savior cares about the difference between lips and hearts?
Which is harder for you personally: saying you follow Him, or showing it when no one is keeping track?

segments.name: Six-word scripture race
steps: Form teams of two or three. Using their scriptures or phones, each team looks up the four references on the board.
For each one, the team writes a summary of exactly six words that answers this: what does taking His name involve?
After five minutes, have teams read their summaries for each verse. Let the class vote by applause for the clearest one for each reference.
Point out what the verses share: Elder Fantone says taking the Savior’s name requires a lifelong determination to serve Him, and that we serve Him by serving the people around us.
questions: According to Mosiah 5:13, can you really know someone you have never served? Why or why not?

segments.name: Time did not change
steps: Tell the missionary story honestly. As a mission president, Elder Fantone met with some missionaries in their first months who were in tears, sad, lonely, and homesick, not sure they could last three more months. Read the third key quote below to show what they did next.
Continue: a year later the same missionaries came in with glowing faces, loving the people and the work, and wishing time would slow down. Read the fourth key quote below.
Discuss the questions below. Do not rush; these are questions youth really ask.
Read President Romney’s words from the aligned quotes. Ask what it would mean if service is what heaven is made of, and not only a way to get there.
questions: Is it fake to serve when you do not feel like it? What does the missionaries’ experience say about that?
What do you think actually changed inside those missionaries, and who changed it?
When have you gone to serve grudgingly and come home different?

segments.name: The Anyway Challenge
steps: Briefly share how Elder Fantone learned this at home: his parents gave up the boys’ room for a student who could not afford housing near his school, and later the girls’ room for children who needed a safe place to stay.
Read the quote from President Farnes in the aligned quotes.

Explain the challenge, which is your application of the talk: this week, pick one person and one real act of service. Pray first, then do it anyway, whether or not you feel like it, as the missionaries did.
Give two minutes of silent writing. On a fresh side of the card each youth writes a name, an act, and a day. They keep the card in their scriptures or take a photo of it.
questions: Who is right in front of you this week, at home, at school, or in this room?

segments.name: Witness and follow-up
steps: As a quick check, ask each youth to tell a neighbor in one sentence what taking His name means.
Read Elder Fantone’s testimony from the talk: as we lose our lives in the Savior’s service, we will find Him and we will find ourselves. Add your own witness.
Tell them that next week you will start class by asking two things: what did you do, and did anything change in you?

key_quotes.text: The Savior’s invitation is not merely for us to add His name to our name like a badge of religious affiliation.
His invitation is for us to take upon us His name. It is an invitation to become more like Him through covenant keeping.
Yet these valiant missionaries got on their knees, put on their name tags, and went out to serve anyway.
Time did not change—the missionaries did.

scriptures.use: Team race: read it and write a six-word summary of what the Savior says we must do with His name.
Team race: look for what people were determined to do when they were baptized, and for how long.
Team race: summarize in six words who we are really serving when we help another person.
Team race, then discuss together: how do we come to know the Master?

aligned_quotes.text: Service is not something we endure on this earth so we can earn the right to live in the celestial kingdom. Service is the very fiber of which an exalted life in the celestial kingdom is made
aligned_quotes.speaker: President Marion G. Romney
President Farnes
aligned_quotes.text: Let us put compassion into action and minister to the person in front of us.

takeaways: Taking the Savior’s name is not a badge I wear; it is a covenant I live.
I serve Jesus Christ by lifting, loving, and serving the people around me.
When I serve even though it is hard, the work may stay the same, but He changes me.
act: Do your Anyway Challenge: one person, one act of service, on the day you wrote down. Pray before you go.
As the sacrament prayers are said this Sunday, listen for the words about His name and decide one way you will show it at school on Monday.
Make room for someone: a seat at your table, a place in your group, a spot in your conversation.
Tell a parent or leader what you did and what you noticed in yourself.
adapt: At home or with one or two youth: skip the voting. Each person writes a six-word summary for two verses and you compare.
Large class: assign each team only one reference so every verse is covered in less time.
Short on time: keep Sign here, the missionary story, and the Anyway Challenge.

children.title: When I Help Others, I Serve Jesus
children.big_idea: When I help others, I serve Jesus.
children.objective: Children will be able to say that helping others is a way to serve Jesus Christ and will choose one way to help someone this week.
prepare: Read the part of Elder Fantone’s talk about his parents sharing their home.
Bring a soft ball, paper, and crayons.
Bring building blocks, or three sheets of paper to lay on the floor as rooms.
Write on the board: When I help others, I serve Jesus.

segments.name: Roll the ball, say your name
steps: Sit in a circle. After a prayer, roll the ball to a child. That child says his or her name and rolls the ball to someone else, until everyone has had a turn.
Tell the children that every name is special, and that today they will learn about the most special name of all, the name of Jesus Christ.
Say that they will learn how to show that they love Jesus and want to follow Him.

segments.name: A house with room to share
steps: Build a little house with three rooms from blocks, or lay three papers on the floor. Explain that Elder Fantone, a leader in the Church, grew up in a small house with three bedrooms: one for the boys, one for the girls, and one for the parents.

Tell the story simply. A young man needed a place to stay so he could go to school. The parents let him use the boys’ room. Another time some children needed a safe place to stay. The parents let them use the girls’ room.
Let children take turns standing in a room and then moving over to make room while everyone says: Come in, there is room.
Tell them Elder Fantone believes his parents would gladly have given up their own room if Mary and Joseph had knocked on their door.
questions: How do you think the people felt when the family made room for them?
Who were the parents really helping?

segments.name: Say it and move
steps: Open the scriptures to Mosiah 2:17. Explain that a good king named Benjamin taught that when we help other people, we are helping God.
Teach the truth on the board with actions: When I help others (reach both hands out), I serve Jesus (place hands over heart).
Repeat it several ways: whispering, standing tall, crouching low, marching in place.
Tell them what Elder Fantone taught: Jesus invites us to love and help the people around us.

segments.name: Helping charades
steps: Whisper a way to help to one child, who acts it out without words while the others guess. Ideas: picking up toys, sharing crayons, carrying something for someone, sitting by someone who is alone, opening a door, comforting someone who is sad.
After each guess, everyone says the truth with its actions: When I help others, I serve Jesus.
Give every child who wants one a turn.
questions: How do you feel inside when you help someone?

segments.name: My helping hand
steps: Give each child paper and crayons. Help them trace one hand.
Inside the hand, each child draws one way to help someone this week, at home, at church, or with a friend.
Help them write, or write for them, at the top: I can serve Jesus.
Invite a few children to show their drawing and tell about it.

segments.name: Sing
steps: Sing I’m Trying to Be like Jesus or Jesus Said Love Everyone together. Add simple actions if the children enjoy them.
Ask the question below after singing.
questions: What does this song say we can do to be like Jesus?

segments.name: I will help
steps: Ask each child to finish this sentence aloud: This week I will help...
Say the truth together one last time with the actions.
Share your testimony that Jesus Christ lives and that we feel close to Him when we help others.
Tell the children that next week you will ask them to tell how they helped. Send the drawings home.

key_quotes.text: Taking upon us His name requires a lifelong determination to serve Him.
His invitation is for us to take upon us His name by covenant and to serve Him with all our heart, might, mind, and strength—by lifting, loving, and serving our fellow men.

scriptures.use: Show the verse and explain it in simple words; older children read it aloud. Use it to teach that helping others is helping God.
For older children: read aloud and find what people promised to do when they were baptized.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Farnes
aligned_quotes.text: Let us put compassion into action and minister to the person in front of us.

takeaways: I show that I love Jesus by helping others.
When I help others, I serve Jesus Christ.
I can make room for others and be kind.
act: Do the helping idea you drew inside your hand.
Make room for someone: share a seat, a toy, or a turn.
Tell your family at dinner or bedtime how you helped, and say together: When I help others, I serve Jesus.
music: I'm Trying to Be like Jesus

adapt.younger: Ages 3-7: keep the story to a few sentences and let the children move between the rooms. Use only easy charades, and act them out together with a helper. Repeat the one truth with actions many times. An adult can write on each drawing.
adapt.older: Ages 8-11: have a child read Mosiah 2:17 and another read Moroni 6:3 aloud. Ask how serving others helps us keep the promise we make at baptism to take the name of Jesus Christ upon us. Let an older child lead the charades.
